_README: Explicit human arbitration between overlays that disagree about an answer.
Applied LAST by build_bank.py -- after solved-html, which is otherwise the
final word -- so a recorded decision cannot be silently undone by a later
round. Keyed by '<paper>::q<num>', the same form adjudicate/_resolved.json
uses, so the two files read together.
WHY THIS EXISTS. build_bank.py already refuses to ship when an adjudicated
verdict is overwritten by a later overlay, and it was doing exactly that on
four questions. restale re-solves questions whose SOURCE TEXT was repaired;
on these four the repair did not restore the missing figure, so restale
re-derived an answer from the same broken input and, in 3 of the 4, landed
on precisely the answer adjudication had recorded as supersededAnswerIndex
-- the one it had explicitly rejected. Reordering the overlays would flip 9
answers at once, 5 of which are legitimately decided by solved-html, so the
contested cases are recorded here instead: one line each, with the reason.
FIELDS:
answerIndex   the winning option, 0-3. Use null to WITHDRAW the answer
entirely (ships answerIndex -1, 'never attempted') -- the
right call when the question is unanswerable from source
and every overlay's answer was a placeholder.
confidence    optional. Carry the confidence the source files recorded.
It is NOT optional in practice: answerConfidence drives the
bank's count of weak answers needing review, so omitting it
makes an arbitrated question vanish from that tally and look
stronger than it is. On an entry that decides only text or a
note it also works the other way: set it to pull a flagged
question back into the tally. See the q79 entry, which is
badged 'high' by its solver and would otherwise never be looked
at by the one person who needs to look at it.
reason        shown to the reader in the bank's disputeNote.
question      optional. A repaired stem, verbatim from the scan. Use when
the OCR stem is damaged, not merely ugly.
options      optional. A repaired option list, verbatim from the scan.
Required whenever the options themselves are unreadable:
choosing the right INDEX out of four strings of garbage is
not choosing the right answer, and the reader would still
be shown the garbage. The build fails if a repaired option
list leaves the answer pointing outside it.
note          optional. A warning for the reader, appended to disputeNote,
for a question whose ANSWER is not in doubt but which the
reader should treat with care -- an under-determined puzzle,
say. Applied on its own: an entry carrying only a note
changes nothing else, and that is the point.
evidence      optional. Where the decision was checked, and how.
ANSWERLESS ENTRIES ARE NOT THE SAME THING. An entry with NO answerIndex key
at all decides only text and/or a note; the answer is left exactly as the
overlays produced it. That is DIFFERENT from answerIndex: null, which
withdraws the answer and ships 'never attempted'. The first draft of this
build treated both as withdrawals and silently stripped four good answers
from questions whose only problem was a damaged stem. If you mean to
withdraw, write the null out loud.
NO OFFICIAL KEY EXISTS for any of these four sittings. Verified against both
the corpus (../mpsc-question-bank/pdfs/Answer_Keys/, 196 PDFs) and the 194
ingested papers in state/official-answer-keys.json. The only UDC/Assistant key
in the corpus is the April-2024 sitting, which is the one already used to
measure solved-html at 158/159. So none of this can be checked against a
published answer: every entry rests on the reasoning recorded in the source
files, not on authority.
RE-VERIFY BEFORE TRUSTING. Three of the four have now been read off the
source scans rather than reasoned about; q100 could not be. The papers are
image-only with no text layer, so the method is pdftoppm to a render plus
tesseract over ink-profile crops -- the figures themselves are not
machine-readable, and for q100 they are destroyed in the scan outright.
Each entry below carries an `evidence` block naming the page and how it
was read, so a later reader can repeat the check instead of trusting it.
checked against a published answer. Every entry below rests on the reasoning
recorded in the source files, not on authority. Re-verify against the scans
before treating any of it as settled.

LDC under MPSC Paper-II 2025.::q100.reason: The four dice positions printed on this question scan as a solid black block, so the face opposite 2 cannot be derived from the paper at all. Adjudication called this 'unresolved' and still carried an index; restale produced a different index from the same absent figure. Both were placeholders, so neither is shipped: an unsupported guess on a reasoning item is worse than an honest blank, and this question is already flagged figureBased and held out of scored tests.

evidence.source: ~/hello-rescue/2/ldc-under-mpsc-paper-ii-2025.pdf, page 12 (the paper is image-only, no text layer)
evidence.method: pdftoppm -r 400 and -r 130 renders, then tesseract at psm 4/6/11/12 over the figure crop, with and without contrast stretch
evidence.finding: every OCR mode returns noise; an ink-column profile finds ONE connected cluster spanning x 418-1923 rather than four separate dice, so no pip structure survives. The figure is destroyed in the scan, not merely hard to read.

LDC under MPSC Paper-II 2025.::q95.question: Find the missing character from among the given alternatives. Table: row 1 = K, B; row 2 = G, ?
LDC under MPSC Paper-II 2025.::q95.reason: Confirmed against the scan. The figure is a 2x2 grid with a vertical divider -- K | B over G | ? -- read at 400 dpi (the '?' OCRs as '2'). Using alphabet positions K=11, B=2, G=7: the row sum K+B = 13 is constant, so G+? = 13 gives ? = 6 = F, option (d), index 3. This is the ONLY consistent rule of the four candidates -- equal column sums want ?=16, equal diagonals want ?=-2, equal products want a non-integer -- so the answer does not depend on guessing which pattern was intended. Adjudication's derivation and this read agree; restale's rests only on the figure being absent from the extract and is a guess by its own explanation.

evidence.method: pdftoppm -r 400, ink-profile crops of each grid row, tesseract psm 6/7/11
evidence.check: row sums 11+2=13 and 7+6=13; column sums 11+7=18 vs 2+6=8 disagree, diagonals and products give no valid letter, which is what makes 13 the intended rule
evidence.grid: K | B over G | ? -- confirmed by the printed rules: two vertical rules at x=504 and x=824 give exactly two columns, and the two text bands give two rows

LDC under MPSC Paper-II 2025.::q96.question: Find the missing character from among the given alternatives. Table: row 1 = C, F, I; row 2 = ?, O, L
LDC under MPSC Paper-II 2025.::q96.reason: TEXT ONLY -- this entry deliberately has no answerIndex, so it repairs the stem and leaves the answer alone. The linearizer had flattened this 3x2 grid to 'C | F | I ? | O | L', which does not say which letters share a row: read as a row it is wrong, read as columns it is right. The 'Table: row 1 = ...' form is the one the vision correction recorded, and it is unambiguous.

evidence.method: located the printed rules by ink profile, then OCR'd each of the six cells separately
evidence.grid: vertical rules at x=425/719/1013/1305 give three columns; horizontal rules at y=2701/2810/2919 give two rows; all six cells read C F I over ? O L
evidence.answer: unchanged and untouched by this entry

LDC under MPSC Paper-II 2025.::q92.question: Directions: In the question below are given two statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given two statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given two statements, disregarding commonly known facts: Statements I. All men are dogs. II. All dogs are cats. Conclusions I. All men are cats. II. All cats are men.
LDC under MPSC Paper-II 2025.::q92.reason: TEXT ONLY, no answerIndex. An upstream cleanup stripped the ']]- Directions (Question No. 92):' preamble as boilerplate, on the reasonable grounds that it is shared by a block of questions. In a standalone question bank that is not boilerplate, it is the question: the shipped answer is 'If only conclusion I follows', which holds ONLY because the directions tell the reader to take 'All men are dogs' as true. A reader using real-world knowledge instead picks 'If neither I nor II follows', and concludes the bank is wrong. The directions are restored, with the OCR damage repaired (I. for TI., II. for IL., 'two' for 'twe').

evidence.method: the directions block was recovered from this repo's own history at commit 905637e, where it was still attached to the question, and cross-checked against the 400 dpi render
evidence.answer: unchanged (index 0) and still correct BECAUSE the directions are present

UDC Combined Paper-II (B) May-2025.::q79.note: FLAG, NOT A CORRECTION: the clues as printed do not single out one option. Reading the stem as four people (A, B, C, D) around a table, each holding one distinct trade, and applying all four clues, three of the printed options survive -- (b) Tailor and Cook, (c) Barber and Cook and (d) Washer man and Cook. The answer does not depend on which way 'right of' is taken. The answer shown is index 3, which is consistent with the clues but not forced by them, so treat this one as untested rather than as a keyed answer.
UDC Combined Paper-II (B) May-2025.::q79.reason: NOTE ONLY -- deliberately no answerIndex, so this entry changes nothing but the warning the reader sees. The answer changed from index 1 to index 3 between two rebuilds with no new evidence: both are consistent with the printed clues, and the puzzle as transcribed is under-determined, so neither is demonstrably right. Recording which index happens to be shipped would give the accident a standing it has not earned.

evidence.method: brute force over all 4! seatings x 4! trade assignments, keeping only those satisfying all four clues
evidence.result: 40 surviving assignments, giving 5 distinct (trade of A, trade of B) pairs; three of them are printed options
evidence.open: the stem is OCR-damaged -- the clue numbers came through as 'IL', 'IH' and '1V' -- so a clue may have been lost in transcription. Re-read the page image before trusting or replacing this answer.
evidence.answer: left as the build produced it, index 3, unverified

UDC ARC Paper-I::q2.reason: 'The prices are up' -- 'up' follows the linking verb 'are' and predicates a state, which is the adjective sense; dictionaries list 'prices are up' under it. restale read the same absence of an object as adverbial, but that reasoning would make almost any predicate adjective an adverb, and it contradicts how the word is classified after a copula. Adjudication marked this 'changed' at high confidence, having examined it specifically because it disagreed with the first solve.

UDC Combined Paper-II (B) May-2025.::q36.question: 10 books each of ₹ 300 are sold at ₹ 2500. What is the percentage of the discount given?
UDC Combined Paper-II (B) May-2025.::q36.reason: Read off the scan at 600 dpi, not reconstructed. 10 x 300 = 3000 marked price, sold for 2500, so the discount is 500 and 500/3000 = 1/6 = 16 2/3%. The printed options are stacked mixed fractions, which OCR flattened into one line of punctuation; reading the numerators and denominators separately off the render gives (a) 11 1/5 %, (b) 17 4/10 %, (c) 16 2/3 %, (d) 16 17/20 % -- so 16 2/3% is option (c), index 2. This CORRECTS the earlier entry, which had guessed index 0 by assuming the OCR fragments '17 1/2%' and '20%' were whole options. The question stem is also repaired: the parser had appended its failed fraction-flattening attempt to the stem as trailing garbage.

evidence.method: pdftoppm -r 600, then per-option ink-profile crops read as text art and cross-checked with tesseract
evidence.crossCheck: the correct value 16 2/3% occurs exactly once among the four printed options, and the arithmetic is exact
